αἰγίσθοιο: Αἴγισθος — Aegisthus, seducer of Clytemnestra and killer of Agamemnon, later killed by Orestes; gen. sg.
αἰγίσθου: Αἴγισθος — Aegisthus, seducer of Clytemnestra and killer of Agamemnon; gen. sg.
αἰχμητάων: αἰχμητής — spearman, warrior; masc. gen. pl., epic -άων (= Attic -ῶν)
αἱ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. nom. pl. ’they’, referring to the ships (αἱ δ’ ... ἔπλεον) · also fem. nom. pl. ’they’, of women (αἱ δ’ ὅτε ... ἵκοντο ’and when they came’) · also fem. nom. pl. ’they’, of the mules (αἱ δ’ ὦκα λίπον ’and they quickly left’) · also fem. nom. pl. ’they’, of the islands (αἱ δέ τ’ ἄνευθε ’and they lie apart’) · also fem. nom. pl. with a noun, article-like: ’the others’ (αἱ ἄλλαι ’the other ships’) · also fem. nom. pl., correlative, of the doors: αἱ μὲν … αἱ δ’ ’the one … the other’ · also fem. nom. pl. ’they’, of the swine (αἱ δὲ νέμονται ’and they graze’) · also fem. nom. pl. with a noun, article-like: ’the’ (αἱ κύνες ’the dogs’) · also fem. nom. pl., correlative, of the maids: αἱ μὲν … αἱ δ’ ’some … others’, in orders ’some of you … others of you’ · also fem. nom. pl. ’they’, of the cattle (αἱ μὲν γίγνονται ’they grow’) · also fem. nom. pl., correlative, of the Achaean women: αἱ μὲν … αἱ δ’ ’some … others’
αἴαντός: Αἴας — Ajax, the Greek hero; masc. gen. sg.
αὐτοῖσι: αὐτός — self; masc./neut. dat. pl.: ’for them, to them’ (dat. of persons served)
αὐτὰρ: αὐτάρ — but, and then; epic conj. (= Attic δέ, ἀλλά)
αὐτῷ: αὐτός — self; masc. dat. sg.: ’himself’, reinforcing a personal pronoun (σοὶ δ’ αὐτῷ ’to you yourself’) · also used alone as a plain personal pronoun, ’him’, not reinforcing anything (ἐπ’ αὐτῷ μηχανόωνται ’are plotting against him’) · also with a noun, ’own, very’, in the dat. of accompaniment: αὐτῷ φάρει ’with the cloak itself, cloak and all’ · also reinforcing a 1st-person pronoun: ’myself’ (ἐμοὶ αὐτῷ) · also plain pronoun of a thing, ’it’, after a preposition (ἀμφ’ αὐτῷ ’around it’)
αὖτε: αὖτε — again, in turn, on the other hand; adv.
βασιλῆος: βασιλεύς — king; masc. gen. sg., epic -ῆος (= Attic -έως)
βουλή: βουλή — plan, counsel, will; nom. sg.
βοὴ: βοή — shout, cry; fem. nom. sg.
βοῦς: βοῦς — ox, cow; pl. ’cattle’; acc. pl. · also masc./fem. nom. sg. (same spelling as the acc. pl.): ’the ox, the heifer’ (ἦλθε ... βοῦς ’the heifer came’)
γ: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle (elided γ’)
γένηται: γίγνομαι — come to be, happen; aor. subj. 3 sg., in a temporal clause with ἄν/κε: ’shall come’ · also aor. subj. 3 sg. in a direct question of doubt/deliberation, no ἄν/κε: τί … γένηται; ’what is to happen?’ · also aor. subj. 3 sg., prospective in a negative statement with a relative clause: οὐδὲ γένηται ’nor ever shall there be’ · also aor. subj. 3 sg. in a general relative clause without ἄν/κε: ’whatever shall come to pass’ (ὅσσα γένηται) · also aor. subj. 3 sg. in a fear clause after μή: ’lest it become’ (μή … ἕλωρ … γένηται ’lest it become prey’) · also aor. subj. 3 sg. in an indirect clause after ὅπως: ’(consider) how it may turn out’ (ὅπως ὄχ’ ἄριστα γένηται) · also aor. subj. 3 sg. with κε, in a conditional or relative clause: ’shall prove, become’ (ὁππότερος … κε νικήσῃ κρείσσων τε γένηται; αἴ κέν … γένηται)
γέροντος: γέρων — old man, elder; masc. gen. sg. (ἁλίοιο γέροντος ’of the old man of the sea’, θείοιο/τοῖο γέροντος ’of the divine/that old man’, epithets of Proteus) · also of an ordinary old man, with παλαιοῦ: ’of an aged old man’ · also ἁλίοιο γέροντος of Phorcys, the same epithet ’of the old man of the sea’ · also in apposition to a name: ’the old man’ (Λαέρταο γέροντος ’of the old man Laertes’)
γε: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle
γλυκερῷ: γλυκερός — sweet; masc./neut. dat. sg. (ὕπνῳ γλυκερῷ ’sweet sleep’)
δέμας: δέμας — bodily form, frame; neut. acc. sg., accusative of respect: ’in body’ · also neut. acc. sg., direct object or in apposition: ’body’ (εἶδός τε δέμας τε ’form and body’)
δή: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δήμῳ: δῆμος — district, land, people; dat. sg.
δαναοὶ: Δαναοί — the Danaans, one of Homer’s names for the Greeks; masc. nom. pl.
δαναῶν: Δαναοί — the Danaans, the Greeks; masc. gen. pl.
διάκτορος: διάκτορος — the guide; standing epithet of Hermes, masc. nom. sg.; sense not actually known (’the guide’ is a conventional gloss)
διὶ: Ζεύς — Zeus, chief of the gods; masc. dat. sg.
δῆμον: δῆμος — people, land, community; masc. acc. sg.
δῶκε: δίδωμι — give; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔδωκε)
εἰ: εἰ — if; conditional conj. · also introducing an indirect question after a verb of asking or telling: ’whether’ (εἰ δή ’whether indeed’) · also in εἰ δ’ ἄγε, an interjectional idiom with the imperative: ’come now, well then’ · also with opt., in a wish: ’if only’ (εἰ … ὁμοφρονέοις … γένοιο) · also ὡς εἰ + opt., ’as if’ (ὡς εἰ … ἱκοίατο ’as if they had come’) · also ὡς εἰ, ’as if’, before a noun with no verb of its own (ὡς εἰ κέρα … ἠὲ σίδηρος ’as if horn or iron’)
εἰδώς: οἶδα — know; perf. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’knowing’
εἴδωλα: εἴδωλον — phantom, shade, image; neut. nom. pl.
εἴη: εἰμί — be; pres. opt. 3 sg.: ’it might be, he might be’; impersonal + inf.: ’it might be possible for him’ · also in a wish with a dat. of the person: ’may there be (for us)’ (εἴη μὲν νῦν νῶϊν … ἐδωδὴ ’may there be food for us two’) · also in a wish after εἰ γάρ, ’if only (all things) were’ · also in a fear clause after μή, ’lest it be (a god)’ · also in a conditional protasis: ’if he were’ (εἰ τοιόσδ’ εἴη) · also in an indirect question after a past verb: ’who he was’ (τίς εἴη) · also in a negative wish with μή, ’may (no man) be’ · also potential opt. with κε in a relative clause, ’which would be’ (τό κε κέρδιον εἴη ’which would be better’) · also in a wish after αἲ γάρ, with a perf. pass. part.: ’would that it were (fulfilled)’ (αἲ γὰρ … τετελεσμένον εἴη) · also pres. opt. 3 sg. in a relative clause standing for a condition: ’(a man) who were’ (ὅς τ’ ἄλκιμος εἴη ’one who were valiant’)
εἵμαρτο: μείρομαι — receive a share; pluperf. 3 sg. impersonal εἵμαρτο: ’it was fated’, + acc. and inf.
εἵματα: εἷμα — garment, clothing; neut. acc. pl. · also neut. nom. pl., subject: εἵματα γάρ ῥ’ ἐβάρυνε ’for the clothes weighed him down’
εἶδός: εἶδος — form, appearance, beauty; neut. acc. sg.; accented before enclitic τε
εὐρώεντα: εὐρώεις — mouldy, dank, dark (traditional gloss, uncertain); masc. acc. sg.
εὗρον: εὑρίσκω — find; aor. 3 pl., unaugmented (= ηὗρον) · also aor. 1 sg.: ’I found’ (εὗρον ἔπειτ’ … ἑταίρους)
ζεὺς: Ζεύς — Zeus, king of the gods; nom. sg.
θ: τε (elided and aspirated θ’ before rough breathing, cf. ἔφαθ’) — and; connective particle · also with the relative ὅθι, no connective force: ὅθι θ’ ’where’ · also epic τε after a relative, no connective force (οὕς θ’ ’which’) · also epic τε after οὐδέ, no connective force: οὐδέ θ’ ἅλεσσι ’nor … with salt’
θάνον: θνῄσκω — die; aor. 3 pl., unaugmented (= ἔθανον): ’they died’
θέλγει: θέλγω — enchant, bewitch, beguile; pres. 3 sg.
θανάτῳ: θάνατος — death; masc. dat. sg., dat. of means: ’by a (pitiful) death’ · also dat. after ἐοικώς ’like’: ’like death’ (θανάτῳ ἄγχιστα ἐοικώς ’most like death’)
θανόντος: θνῄσκω — die; aor. part. masc. gen. sg. (aor. ἔθανον): ’dead’, lit. ’having died’
θανὼν: θνῄσκω — die; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having died, now dead’
θεοὶ: θεός — god; nom. pl. · also voc. pl. (same form): ’you gods!’
θεοῖσιν: θεός — god; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι(ν) (= Attic -οις)
θερμὰ: θερμός — hot, warm; adj., neut. acc. pl. (agreeing with δάκρυα) · also neut. nom. pl., agreeing with λοετρά: ’warm baths’
θεσπεσίη: θεσπέσιος — divinely wonderful, marvellous; fem. nom. sg., Ionic η (= Attic θεσπεσία)
θεσπεσίοιο: θεσπέσιος — wondrous, marvellous, divinely great; masc./neut. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= -ου)
θυμῷ: θυμός — heart, spirit, soul; dat. sg.
θῆκε: τίθημι — put, place, make; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔθηκε)
κ: κε(ν) (elided κ’) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + subj. in a general relative: ’whoever’ (ὃς δέ κ’ … ἵκηται ’whoever comes’) · also + opt., potential: ’would’ (καί κ’ ἐλθὼν … εἴποιμι ’and I would go and tell’) · also + aor. indic., unreal past: ’would have’ (καί νύ κ’ … ἔδυ ’and … would have set’) · also + fut. indic. in a main clause: ’will’ (τοὺς δέ κ’ … θέλξει ’and then … will enchant them’) · also + subj. in the protasis after εἰ: ’if ever’ (εἰ μέν κ’ αἰνήσωσι ’if they approve’) · also + opt. in the protasis after εἴ: ’if perhaps’ (τόν κ’ εἴ μοι δοίης ’if you would give me him’) · also + subj. in the protasis after αἴ: ’if perhaps’ (αἴ κ’ αὐτὸν γνώω ’if I come to know him’) · also + subj. in a purpose clause after ὄφρα: ’so that’ (ὄφρα κ’ … ἐρεθίζω ’so that I may provoke’) · also + subj. in a purpose clause after ὥς: ’so that’ (ὥς κ’ … ἵκηται ’so that he may reach’) · also + subj. in the protasis after αἴ: ’if you should wish’ (αἴ κ’ ἐθέλῃσθα)
κέ: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν); accented before an enclitic · also + subj. in a purpose clause after ὄφρα: ’so that’ (ὄφρα κέ τοι λύσῃ ’so that she may free’) · also + subj. in the protasis after αἴ: ’if perhaps’ (αἴ κέ ποθι Ζεὺς δώῃ ’if Zeus should somehow grant’) · also + subj. in the protasis after εἴ: ’if perhaps’ (εἴ κέ τιν’ … εὕρωμεν ’if we should find any’) · also + opt. in the protasis after αἴ: ’if perhaps’ (αἴ κέ μοι … παρασταίης ’if you would stand by me’) · also + aor. indic., unreal past: τῷ κέ με … ὤνησεν ’would have benefited me’ · also + fut./short-vowel aor. subj. in a main clause: κέ τοι καταλέξω ’I shall tell you’ · also + opt. in the protasis after εἴ: ’if perhaps’ (εἴ κέ μιν ἀγγείλαιμι ’if I might report him’) · also + subj. after εἰς ὅ, ’until’ (εἰς ὅ κέ τοι φήνωσι ’until they show you’) · also + subj. in a prospective relative clause: ’who shall’ (ὅς κέ με κεῖσ’ ἀγάγῃ ’who shall lead me there’) · also + fut. indic. (or short-vowel subj.) in a clause after εἴ: ’whether perhaps’ (εἴ κέ σφι … τελευτήσει ’whether … it will come to pass for them’) · also + opt., potential, in a main clause: ’might’ (καί κέ τεο … πειρηθεῖμεν ’we might test any of’) · also + impf. indic., unreal past: ‘would have been’ (καί κέ τοι … ἀμφεπονεῖτο ‘would have been busy for you’) · also + opt. in a relative clause: ‘from where you would’ (ὅθεν κέ τοι … ἄλφοι)
κέλευθα: κέλευθος — path, way, course; neut. nom./acc. pl. κέλευθα, epic by-form beside fem. sg. κέλευθος
κέν: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν); accented before an enclitic · also + aor. indic., unreal past: κέν μοι … κατέχευας ’you would have poured on me’ · also + subj. in a main clause: ’may’ (καί κέν οἱ ὑπέρσχῃ χεῖρα ’and he may hold his hand over him’) · also + opt., potential: ’would’ (κέν μοι … εἴη ’would be mine’) · also + subj. in the protasis after αἴ: ’if perhaps’ (αἴ κέν τις … ὀρέξῃ ’if perhaps someone holds out’) · also + subj. in a temporal clause: ’whenever’ (ὅτε κέν … μεταλλῶσιν ’whenever they ask’) · also + opt., potential, in a clause with ὅ ’that’: ’might’ (ὅ κέν τις … ἀμύνοι ’that someone might defend’) · also + opt. in a purpose clause after ὥς: ’so that … would’ (ὥς κέν τις φαίη ’so that anyone would say’)
κίον: κίω — go, move; epic impf. 3 pl. (= ἐπορεύοντο), unaugmented · also κίων — pillar, column; masc. acc. sg., elided (κίον’ = κίονα): ’pillar’ (κίον’ ἀν’ ὑψηλήν ’up the tall pillar’)
καλὴν: καλός — beautiful, fair; fem. acc. sg.
καλὸν: καλός — beautiful, fair, fine; masc. acc. sg. (agreeing with a noun) · also neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’beautifully’ (with an infinitive) · also neut. acc. sg. used as a noun, direct object: ’a fine one’ (μάλα καλὸν ἑλών) · also neut. acc. sg., attributive, agreeing with a stated neut. noun: ’fine’ (καλὸν δέπας ’the fine cup’) · also neut. nom. sg., agreeing with ὕδωρ: ’fair, fine’ (ὕδωρ καλὸν ’fair water’) · also neut. acc. sg., adverbial or cognate with a finite verb: οὐ καλὸν ἔειπες ’you have not spoken well’ · also neut. nom. sg., predicate with an infinitive as subject: ’a fine thing (to hear)’
καλῇ: καλός — beautiful, fair, fine; fem. dat. sg.
καμόντων: κάμνω — toil, grow weary; aor. part. masc. gen. pl.: βροτῶν καμόντων ’of mortals who have toiled’, i.e. the dead
κατ: κατά (elided κατ’) — down from, throughout; + gen./acc. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (κατ’ … ἕζετο = κατέζετο ’sat down’) · also + acc., of place, ’along’ (κατ’ ἠερόεντα κέλευθα ’along the misty paths’) · also + acc., ‘over against’ (κατ’ ἄντηστιν ‘right opposite’)
κατάγων: κατάγω — lead down, bring in; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’bringing’
κατέθηκε: κατατίθημι — put down, put away, store; aor. 3 sg. (κ-aorist) ’put away’
κατέρυκε: κατερύκω — hold back, detain; pres. imper. 2 sg. (with μή: ’stop holding back’) · also impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= Attic κατήρυκε): ’was holding back, tried to hold back’
κε: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + subj. after εἰς ὅ, ’until’ (εἰς ὅ κε … ἐποτρύνῃ ’until … urges on’) · also + subj. in a general relative: ’whoever’ (ὅς κε πίῃ) · also + subj. in a temporal clause: ’whenever, as soon as’ (ὅτε … κε θάνῃσιν; ἐπεί κε … λίπῃ) · also + subj. in a purpose clause after ὄφρα: ’so that’ (ὄφρα κε … ἀκούσῃς) · also + subj. in the protasis after εἰ: ’if ever’ (εἰ δέ κε λίσσηαι ’but if you beg’) · also + aor. indic., unreal past: ’would have’ (καὶ νύ κε … βάλεν ’and she would have hurled’) · also + subj. in a disjunctive statement of what may happen: ’may’ (ἤ κε θάνωμεν ’either we may die’) · also + opt., potential: ’would’ (καί κε … μαχοίμην ’I would fight’) · also + subj. in a relative clause of purpose: ’who are to’ (οἵ κε … ἀγγείλωσι ’who are to announce’) · also + fut. indic. (or short-vowel subj.) in a main clause: ’will’ (αἶψά κε … ἀποτίσεται ’at once he will exact payment’) · also + aor. in a general relative clause: ’who would (decide)’ (οἵ κε … ἔκριναν) · also + opt. in a relative clause: ’whoever might’ (ὅς κε … πόροι ’whoever might offer’) · also + subj. in the protasis after αἴ: ’if perhaps’ (αἴ κε … ἐντανύσῃς) · also + subj. in an indirect clause after ὅττι: ’what … may’ (ὅττι κε κέρδος … ἐγγυαλίξῃ ’what gain … may grant’)
κεν: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + secondary indic. (κατέφθιτο), unreal past conditional: ’would have perished’ · also + aor. indic. of a future event pictured as already accomplished, an eventual near-certainty rather than a counterfactual: ἤ κεν ... κτεῖνεν ’or he may well have killed (him) already’ · also + subj. in a relative clause, prospective: ’who is to, who will’ (ἥ κεν ἄγῃσι ’(a wagon) that shall carry’) · also + opt. in a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὥς κεν … γένοιτο ’so that he might become’) · also + subj. in a temporal clause: ’whenever’ (ὅτε κεν … δαινύῃ ’whenever you feast’) · also + subj. in the protasis of a condition after αἴ: ’if ever’ · also + opt., potential: ’might, may’ · also + opt. in the protasis after εἰ: ’if ever’ (εἰ δέ κεν … ἀφικοίμεθα ’but if we should reach’) · also + fut. indic. or short-vowel subj. in an apodosis: ’will’ (αἶψά κεν … τεύξομεν ’at once we will build’) · also + subj. in the protasis after εἰ: ’if ever’ (εἴ κεν … ἵκωμαι ’if I should come’) · also + subj. in a disjunctive statement of what may happen: ’may’ (ἤ κεν ἁλώῃ ’or he may be caught’) · also + subj. in a general relative: ’whoever’ (ὅς κεν ὀπυίῃ ’whoever marries’) · also + subj. after εἰς ὅ, ’until’ (εἰς ὅ κεν ἔλθω ’until I come’) · also + fut. indic. in a main clause or an indirect disjunctive question: ’shall’ (ἤ κεν … δυνησόμεθ’ ’whether we shall be able’) · also + fut. indic. in a relative clause: ’who will’ (ὅς κεν … ἐποίσει ’who will lay on’) · also + subj. in a purpose clause after ὄφρα: ’so that’ (ὄφρα κεν … καταθείομαι ’so that I may put away’) · also + subj. in a purpose clause after ὥς: ’so that’ (ὥς κεν … πάσχῃ ’so that he may suffer’)
κεῖνα: κεῖνος — that, that one; demonstrative pron., epic (= Attic ἐκεῖνος); neut. acc. pl.: ’those (lands)’ · also neut. acc. pl., ’those things’ (σύας καὶ κεῖνα ’the swine and those things’)
κεῖνον: κεῖνος — that, that one; demonstrative pron., epic (= Attic ἐκεῖνος); masc. acc. sg.
κεῖται: κεῖμαι — lie; pres. 3 sg., used of the dead: ’lies (dead)’ · also in the idiom θεῶν ἐν γούνασι κεῖται: ’rests with the gods, lies in the gods’ hands’ (of an outcome, not of the dead) · also subj. (= κέηται): ’should lie’ · also plain pres. 3 sg. of stored objects: ’lies, is kept/stored’ (κειμήλια κεῖται ’treasures lie stored’) · also pres. 3 sg. of a living person in a settled, ongoing state, not of the dead nor of an outcome nor of stored goods (ὁ μὲν ἐν νήσῳ κεῖται ’πάσχων’): ’remains, is stranded, dwells on’ · also of a place, ’lies, is situated’ (νῆσος ... κεῖται ’an island lies’) · also of an object: ’lies’ (ἀράχνια κεῖται ἔχουσα ’lies holding cobwebs’) · also of the spirit or heart, ’lies sunk (in)’: κεῖται ἐν ἄλγεσι θυμός ’the spirit lies in pains’
κινήσας: κινέω — move, set in motion, shake; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’shaking’
κλέος: κλέος — fame, renown, report; neut. nom. sg. · also neut. acc. sg. (same form), direct object: μέγα κλέος ἤρατο ’won great fame’; κλέος φέρειν ’bring report’
κοῦραι: κούρη — girl, daughter (Attic κόρη); fem. nom. pl. · also fem. voc. pl., in address: κοῦραι Διός ’daughters of Zeus!’
κοῦροι: κοῦρος — young man, boy; nom. pl.
κτείνοντο: κτείνω — kill, slay; impf. 3 pl. mid./pass.: ’were being killed’
λαίλαπι: λαῖλαψ — squall, whirlwind; fem. dat. sg.
λελασμένος: λανθάνω — escape notice; mid. forget (+ acc./gen.); perf. part. mid., masc. nom. sg., epic (= Attic λελησμένος): ’having forgotten’
λεχέεσσι: λέχος — bed, couch; neut. dat. pl., epic -έεσσι
λεύκ: λευκός — white; neut. nom. pl., elided (λεύκ’ = λευκά) · also neut. acc. pl., elided (λεύκ’ = λευκά), agreeing with ὀστέα: ’white’
λυγρὸν: λυγρός — baneful, bitter, grievous; masc. acc. sg.
μάλα: μάλα — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.
μάλιστα: μάλα — very, much; superl. adv. μάλιστα: ’most of all, especially’ · also ’for the most part, mostly’ (μάλιστα ἦμαρ ’the greater part of the day’)
μέγα: μέγας — great, huge; neut. nom./acc. sg. · also neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’greatly’ (μέγα νήπιοι ’greatly foolish’)
μέγαν: μέγας — great, big, tall; masc. acc. sg.
μέγας: μέγας — great, big, grown; masc. nom. sg., predicate: ’grown’ · also plain attributive adj., masc. nom. sg., ’great, huge’ (μέγας σῦς ’a great boar’), not predicate
μέν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ (the acute μέν is kept before a following enclitic; elsewhere μὲν) · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’ (οὐ μέν ’not indeed’) · also μένω — stay, wait; pres. imper. 2 sg., elided (μέν’ = μένε): ’stay’
μέσῳ: μέσος — middle, in the middle of; masc./neut. dat. sg., agreeing with πόντῳ: ’in the middle of the sea’ · also used alone as a noun, ’in the middle’ (ἐν μέσῳ ’in the middle’)
μήσατο: μήδομαι — devise, contrive, plan; aor. mid. 3 sg., unaugmented (= Attic ἐμήσατο)
μετ: μετά (elided μετ’) — among, after, in quest of; prep. + acc. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (μετ’ … βαῖνε = μετέβαινε ’followed’) · also + dat., ’among, between’ (μετ’ ἀμφοτέροισιν ’between the two of them’) · also + gen., ’among, in company with’ (μετ’ ἄλλων … ἑταίρων ’among your other companions’)
μετέειπεν: μετεῖπον — speak among, address a group (poetic aor., defective); aor. 3 sg.: ’spoke among them’
μετὰ: μετά — among, with, after; prep. + dat./acc./gen. · with acc. also ’in quest of, in search of’ (μετὰ χαλκόν ’after bronze’) · also a plain adverb, no case governed: ’besides, in addition’ · also adverb, ’among them, in their midst’: μετὰ δὲ πρέπει ἀγρομένοισιν ’and he stands out among the gathered’ · also as preverb in tmesis (μετὰ … βεβήκει = μεταβεβήκει ’had moved on, passed on’) · also a plain adverb, ’afterwards’ (μετὰ γάρ τε καὶ ἄλγεσι τέρπεται ἀνήρ ’for afterwards a man takes pleasure even in pains’; some take it as ’among’ with ἄλγεσι) · also + dat. of the mind, ’in’ (μετὰ φρεσὶ σῇσι ’in your mind’) · also + dat. of the hands, ’in’ (μετὰ χερσὶν ἐνώμα ’was turning in his hands’)
μοι: ἐγώ — I; encl. dat. sg.: ’to me, for me’ · also dat. of the person affected, ’from my …’ (μοι βλεφάρων ἐξέσσυτο ὕπνος ’sleep rushed out from my eyelids’) · also dat. of possession with εἰμί: ’who are mine’ (οἵ μοι ἔασιν ’who are mine’)
μοῖρ: μοῖρα — fate, portion, lot; fem. nom. sg., elided (μοῖρ’ = μοῖρα)
μοῦσα: Μοῦσα — Muse, goddess of poetic inspiration; voc. sg.
μυχῷ: μυχός — innermost part, corner, recess; masc. dat. sg.
μὲν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’: οὐ μὲν δή ’surely not’
μὴ: μή — not; negative particle in wishes, prohibitions, and purpose/fear clauses · also negating a conditional clause after εἰ: εἰ μὴ ’if not, unless’ · also negating a generic relative clause with the opt.: ὃς μὴ … ἐλάσειε ’whoever did not drive off’ · also ’lest’ in a warning, + 2 sg. fut./subj.: μὴ … ἀποτίσεαι ’lest you pay for it’ · also + inf., negating an infinitive of advice that gives the content of a word: ’not to’ (ἔπος … μὴ πάντα μνηστῆρσιν ὁμιλεῖν ’a word, not to mingle in everything with the suitors’) · also negating a generic relative clause with the subj.: ᾧ μὴ πολλοὶ ἔωσιν ’who has not many’
μῆλα: μῆλον — sheep, goat, flock-animal; neut. nom. pl.: ’the flocks’ · also neut. acc. pl. (same form), direct object: ἦγον ... μῆλα ’they led sheep’
νέοι: νέος — young, new; masc. nom. pl. · also masc. voc. pl., in address: ‘young men!’ (νέοι, ἐκπέμψασθε ‘young men, send out’)
νέστωρ: Νέστωρ — Nestor, king of Pylos; masc. nom. sg.
ναίων: ναίω — dwell, inhabit; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’dwelling’
νόστῳ: νόστος — homecoming, return; masc. dat. sg. (ἐν νόστῳ ’on the way home’)
νύ: νυ — now, then; weak encl. particle
νύκτας: νύξ — night; fem. acc. pl., acc. of time: ’by nights’
νῆας: ναῦς — ship; fem. acc. pl., epic νῆας (= Attic ναῦς)
ξεῖνος: ξεῖνος — stranger, guest-friend (epic = Attic ξένος); nom. sg.
οἰκία: οἰκίον — house, home (Homer only in neut. pl. οἰκία, collective, = Attic οἰκία fem. sg.); neut. acc. pl.
οἰκτίστῳ: οἰκτρός — pitiable, piteous; superlative οἴκτιστος, masc. dat. sg.: ’most pitiable’
οἱ: οἱ — encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him’ (very common) · also ὁ, ἡ, τό ’he, she, it’, masc. nom. pl. ’they’ (e.g. οἱ μὲν … οἱ δέ ’some … others’) · also encl. dat. sg. fem. ’to/for her’ (ἥ οἱ ὁμηλικίη ’who was of an age with her’) · also article-like with a numeral and noun, masc. nom. pl.: ’the’ (οἱ δὲ δύω σκόπελοι ’the two crags’) · also encl. dat. sg. of a thing, ’to/for it’ (δύω δέ τέ οἱ θύραι ’and it has two doors’) · also article-like with a noun, masc. nom. pl.: ’those, the’ (οἱ πέπλοι ’the robes’) · also dat. sg. of the giver with δέχομαι: ’from him’ (οἱ ἐδέξατο ’took from him’)
οἳ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. nom. pl.
οἴκτρ: οἰκτρός — pitiable, piteous; neut. acc. pl. used adverbially, elided (οἴκτρ’ = οἰκτρά): ’piteously’
οἴνῳ: οἶνος — wine; masc. dat. sg., instrumental: ’with wine’ (οἴνῳ βεβαρηότες ’heavy with wine’)
οἷ: οἷος — of what kind, such as; relative/exclamatory adj., neut. nom./acc. pl. οἷα, elided (οἷ’) · also orthotone dat. sg. of the 3rd-person pronoun (= οἱ): ’to him, to her’
οὐδέ: οὐδέ — and not, nor, not even; neg. conj.
οὐδὲ: οὐδέ — and not, nor, not even; neg. conj. (grave, mid-clause form)
οὐλομένης: οὐλόμενος — accursed, destructive, ruinous (perf. part. of ὄλλυμι used as adj.); fem. gen. sg.
οὔ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., in a question expecting the answer ’yes’ · also the plain negative adverb in a declarative statement, with no question implied: ’not’
οὕνεκα: οὕνεκα (crasis of οὗ ἕνεκα) — because; also relative: for the sake of which, for which reason; conj. · also ’that’, introducing what a messenger is to tell (= ὅτι): ἐρέοντα … οὕνεκα ’to tell that’
οὗ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. gen. sg.: ’whose’ (= Attic οὗ) · also neut. gen. sg. in ἐξ οὗ ’since, from the time when’ · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own; masc. gen. sg. agreeing with a noun (οὗ πατρὸς ’her own father’s’)
πάντα: πᾶς — all, every; neut. nom./acc. pl. · also masc. acc. sg.: ’all’ (πάντα δῆμον ’all the people’) · also neut. acc. pl. adverbial: ’altogether, in every respect’ (οὐκ ἄρα πάντα νοήμονες ’not altogether sensible’)
πάντας: πᾶς — all, every; masc. acc. pl.
πάσχομεν: πάσχω — suffer, experience; pres. 1 pl., vivid/generalizing present for a past situation: ‘we suffered’
πέρι: περί — around, about, exceedingly; adv. with anastrophe (accent thrown back): ’beyond all others’ (πέρι κέρδεα οἶδεν) · also preposition with anastrophe + acc., of place: ’around’ (ἄστυ πέρι ’around the city’) · also preposition with anastrophe + gen.: ’about, concerning’ (φόνου πέρι ’about slaughter’)
πίονα: πίων — fat, rich; neut. acc. pl., agreeing with νῶτα: ’fat’ · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with οἶκον: ’rich’
παιδὶ: παῖς — child, son; masc. dat. sg.
παιδὸς: παῖς — child, daughter; fem. gen. sg. (φίλης ... παιδός ’a dear daughter’) · also masc. gen. sg., ’son’ (παιδὸς ἐμοῖο ’my son’; τοῦ παιδὸς ἀγαυοῦ ’the noble son’) · also masc. gen. sg., ’boy, child’, with ἐόντος, gen. of the person described (παιδὸς ἐόντος ’when I was a boy’)
παλαιά: παλαιός — old, of old; neut. acc. pl.: ’things of old’
παναχαιοί: Παναχαιοί — all the Achaeans together (πᾶς + Ἀχαιοί); masc. nom. pl.
παρ: παρά (elided παρ’) — beside, among; + dat. · also + gen., ’from, from the side of’ (παρ’ Ἴλου ’from Ilus’) · also + acc., of motion, ’past, along, beside’ (παρ’ Μίμαντα ’past Mimas’)
πατροκλῆος: Πάτροκλος — Patroclus, Achilles’ companion; masc. gen. sg., epic -ῆος (= Attic -έους)
παῖδα: παῖς — child, son, daughter; masc./fem. acc. sg.
παῦσεν: παύω — stop, check; aor. 3 sg., transitive
περ: περ — even, though; concessive particle, esp. with a participle (= Attic καίπερ) · also used to intensify an adverb or pronoun rather than concede a point: ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’ · also after εἰ, ’if indeed, even if’: εἴ περ γάρ κεν ’if indeed ever’
περικαλλέ: περικαλλής — very beautiful; masc. acc. sg., elided (περικαλλέ’ = περικαλλέα) · also neut. acc./nom. dual, elided (περικαλλέ’ = περικαλλέε), with ὄσσε: ’the two very fair (eyes)’
περικλυτοῦ: περικλυτός — very famous; masc. gen. sg.
περὶ: περί — around, about; prep. + gen.: ’superior to, beyond’; also as adv.: ’exceedingly, surpassingly’ · also prep. + gen. in its plain sense ’about, concerning’ (περὶ πατρός ’about his father’) · also preverb in tmesis · + dat. · also + acc., of place, ’around, about’ (περὶ ἄστυ ’around the city’) · also + gen., of place, physically ’around, encircling’ (περὶ σπείους γλαφυροῖο ’around the hollow cave’), distinct from the comparative ’beyond’ sense above · also + dat. in the fixed idiom περὶ κῆρι ’exceedingly, at heart’ (περὶ κῆρι τιμήσουσιν ’will honor him at heart’) · also + dat., of place, ’around, about’ (περὶ χροῒ ’about the skin’) · also adverb of place, no case: ’round about’ (περὶ δ’ ἕρκος ἐλήλαται ’and round it a fence is driven’) · also + dat., of the thing fought over: ’over, for’ (περὶ κτεάτεσσι μαχειόμενος ’fighting over possessions’)
πηλεΐωνα: Πηλεΐων — son of Peleus, i.e. Achilles; masc. acc. sg., patronymic
πηληϊάδεω: Πηληϊάδης — son of Peleus, i.e. Achilles; masc. gen. sg., epic -εω (= Attic -ου)
πολέμοιο: πόλεμος — war, battle; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
πολέων: πολύς — much, many; masc. gen. pl., uncontracted epic πολέων (= Attic πολλῶν): ’of many’
πολλά: πολύς — much, many; neut. nom. pl. (agreeing with ἔγχεα): ’many’ · also neut. acc. pl., object of a verb: ’many things’ (παλαιά τε πολλά τε εἰδώς ’knowing many old things’) · also neut. acc. pl., adjectival with a noun: ’many’ (πολλά τε δῶρα ’and many gifts’)
πολλοὶ: πολύς — much, many; masc. nom. pl.
πολλὰ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. pl.: ’many things, greatly’ · also neut. nom. pl., plain attributive adj. agreeing with a neut. pl. noun (πολλὰ ... δάκρυα ’many tears’) · also neut. acc. pl., plain attributive adj. (κτήματα πολλὰ ’many possessions’) · also neut. acc. pl. used adverbially: ’again and again’ (πολλὰ περιτροπέοντες) · also neut. nom. pl. as substantive, subject: οἷά τε πολλὰ γίγνεται ’as many things happen’
πολλῷ: πολύς — much, great, many; masc./neut. dat. sg.
πολὺς: πολύς — much, many; masc. nom. sg., grave accent, mid-clause form (χειμὼν πολὺς ’much winter storm’)
ποτ: ποτέ — once, at some time, ever; enclitic adv., elided (ποτ’ = ποτέ)
προσεφώνεε: προσφωνέω — speak to, address; impf. 3 sg., augmented (προσ- + ἐ-φώνεε): ’was speaking to, addressed’
προσεφώνεεν: προσφωνέω — speak to, address; impf. 3 sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic προσεφώνει)
προτέρη: πρότερος — before, first, earlier; fem. nom. sg., predicative: ’first, before (him)’, Ionic η (= Attic προτέρα)
πρόπαν: πρόπας — all through, the whole; neut. acc. sg., of time (πρόπαν ἦμαρ ’all day long’)
πρόσθεν: πρόσθεν — before, in front, formerly; adv. (τὸ πρόσθεν ’in time past, formerly’) · also prep. + gen., ’in front of, before’
πρὸς: πρός — towards, against, to; prep. + acc. · also a plain adverb, no case governed: ’besides, in addition’ · also + dat.: πρὸς ἀλλήλῃσιν ἔχονται ’cling close to one another’ · also + gen., ’from, under the protection of’ (πρὸς Διός εἰσιν ’are from Zeus’) · also + dat., ’against’ (ῥαίοιτο πρὸς οὔδεϊ ’be dashed against the floor’) · also + dat., ’in addition to’ (πρὸς τοῖσί τε ὕπνος ’and sleep in addition to these’) · also + gen., of direction: ’toward, on the side of’ (πρὸς Βορέαο ’toward the North Wind’) · also + gen., in an appeal: ’by (your father)’ (πρὸς πατρὸς γουνάζομαι) · also as preverb in tmesis: με πρὸς μῦθον ἔειπε = με προσέειπε μῦθον ’spoke a word to me’ · also + gen., ’in the eyes of, with’ (πρὸς πόσιός τε καὶ υἱέος ’in the eyes of her husband and son’)
πόντον: πόντος — sea, open sea; acc. sg.
πότμον: πότμος — fate, doom, death; masc. acc. sg.
πὰρ: παρά (apocope πάρ, functioning as an adverb) — beside, alongside; adv. · also a preposition + acc., ’beside’ (πὰρ Νέστορα) · also preverb in tmesis (πὰρ … θῆκεν = παρέθηκε ’set before’) · also a preposition + dat., ’beside’ (πὰρ πυρί ’beside the fire’) · also a preposition + gen., ’from (the side of)’ (πὰρ Ταφίων ’from the Taphians’) · also a preposition + dat., ’among, in the company of’ (πὰρ παύροισι ’among few’)
πᾶσαι: πᾶς — all, every; fem. nom. pl.
σ: σύ — you (sg.); encl. acc. sg., elided (σ’ = σε): ’you’ · also σός — your, yours; neut. nom./acc. pl., elided (σ’ = σά): τὰ σ’ αὐτοῦ κήδε’ ’your own troubles’
σεῖο: σύ — you (sg.); gen. sg., epic σεῖο (= Attic σοῦ) · also gen. of comparison: σεῖο … μακάρτατος ’more blessed than you’
σοὶ: σύ — you (sg.); dat. sg.: ’to, for you’
σφ: σφεῖς — they; epic encl. pron., elided σφ’ for dat. σφι ’for them’ or acc. σφε ’them’
σφιν: σφεῖς — they; epic encl. dat. pl./sg. pron.: ’to/for them’
σὺ: σύ — you (sg.); nom. sg. (grave, mid-clause form)
σὺν: σύν — with, together with; prep. + dat. · also as adverb, ’together’, or as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb: σὺν … κάλυψε = συνεκάλυψε ’covered up’; σὺν … ἔπεσον = συνέπεσον ’fell together, clashed’ · also adverb ’along, with (us)’ construed with ἔχοντες, which takes the object (σὺν … χεῖρας ἔχοντες ’having hands along with us’)
σῷ: σός — your, yours; masc./neut. dat. sg.
τ: τε (elided τ’) — and; ’epic τε’ also marks a standing fact · after οὔ νυ perhaps τοι ’to you’ · also in a question, an expressive epic τε with no connective force, giving a note of doubt or wonder (πῶς τε ...; ’how, pray...?’) · also in ἦ τ’ (= ἦ τε), a strengthened affirmation: ’truly, surely’ (ἦ τ’ ἂν πολὺ κέρδιον ἦεν ’it would surely have been far better’) · also after a relative of size or amount, with no connective force: ὅσην τ’ ὄρεος κορυφήν ’as large as a mountain’s peak’ · also after ἤ ’than’, with no connective force: ἤ τ’ οἰωνοί ’than birds’ · also after ὅ ‘that’, with no connective force: ὅ τ’ οὐκέτι νόστιμός ἐστιν ‘that he is no longer returning’
τί: τίς, τί — who? what?; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially ’why’ · also the enclitic indefinite τις, τι ’someone, something’ (accented τί before an enclitic): neut. acc. sg. used adverbially with a negative, ’at all’ (οὔ τι) · adj. · also plain interrogative, direct object/predicate: ’what’ (τί πάθω ’what am I to suffer’; τί ... γένηται ’what is to become’) · also the enclitic indefinite as an adjective agreeing with a noun, accented before enclitic που: εἴ τί που εἴλυμα ’if any wrapper’ · also enclitic indefinite with a negative, ’anything’, as accusative subject of an infinitive (οὐ … τί φημι κακώτερον ἄλλο … συγχεῦαι ’I say nothing else is worse’) · also enclitic indefinite, adverbial without a negative: ’somehow, in some way’ (τοῦτό τί μοι κάλλιστον ’this seems to me somehow the fairest’) · also enclitic indefinite as an adjective after μή, accented before an enclitic: ’any’ (μή τί τοι … πῆμα ’any harm to you’) · also enclitic indefinite adjective after ὅπως, accented before enclitic μοι: ’any’ (τί … ἄλγος ’any pain’) · also enclitic indefinite adjective after ἤ, accented before the enclitic μοι: ’any’ (ἤ τί μοι … κειμήλιον ’or any treasure of mine’) · also the enclitic indefinite as a substantive object after εἴ: ’anything’ (εἴ τί μιν εἴποι ’whether she would say anything to him’)
ταὶ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. nom. pl., epic (= Attic αἱ): ’they’ · also fem. nom. pl. in a command to the maids, ’you others’ (ταὶ δὲ … ἔρχεσθε) · also with a noun, article-like: ’the’ (ταὶ δὲ γυναῖκες ’and the women’)
τε: τε — and, both...and; enclitic connective; also ’epic τε’ marking a standing general truth in relative clauses
τερπικεραύνῳ: τερπικέραυνος — delighting in the thunderbolt; masc. dat. sg., epithet of Zeus
τεύχεσιν: τεῦχος — armour, gear; neut. dat. pl., ν-movable
τιμῆς: τιμή — honour, worth; fem. gen. sg.
τιν: τις, τι — someone, something; neut./masc. acc. sg., elided (τιν’ = τινα) · also fem. acc. sg. (εἴ τιν’ … λύσιν ’some release’)
τις: τις, τι — someone, something, a certain one; indefinite pron., masc./fem. nom. sg. · also with a negative: ’any, anyone’ (οὐ … τις ’no one’; οὐδέ τις ’nor any’) · also after the relative ὅς, indefinite: ὅς τις ’whichever, whoever’
τοι: σύ — you (sg.); encl. dat. sg.: ’to/for you’ · also τοι, the affirming particle: ’you know, indeed’ (esp. in ἦ τοι, οὔ τοι); the two are not always easy to keep apart
τοιαῦτα: τοιοῦτος — such, of such a kind; demonstr. pron./adj., neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’such things’
τοὺς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. pl. ’them’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom, which; masc. acc. pl. (ἀέθλους, τοὺς … ἐπειρήσαντο Ὀδυσῆος ’the contests with which they tried Odysseus’) · also demonstrative with a noun: masc. acc. pl. ’those, the’ (τοὺς ἄλλους … ἑταίρους ’the rest of my companions’)
τοῖον: τοῖος — such, of such a kind; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’in such a way’ · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a noun or pronoun: ’such a one as’ (σέ γε τοῖον ἐγείνατο ’bore a son such as you’) · also ’so’, qualifying an adj. · also neut. nom./acc. sg., agreeing with a neut. noun: τοῖον … ἔρνος (acc.), τοῖον … δόρυ (nom.) ’such a shoot, such a trunk’
τοῖς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. dat. pl. ’to/among them’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: masc./neut. dat. pl. ’in which, with which’ (τετυγμένα, τοῖς ἐνάμελγεν ’well-made, in which he milked’) · also article-like with a noun, masc. dat. pl.: ’the’ (ἰχθύσι τοῖς ὀλίγοισι ’for the little fishes’) · also demonstrative dat. pl. of things just named, ‘with these’ (τοῖς ἔξειμι ‘with these I shall go out’)
τρόμος: τρόμος — trembling, quaking; masc. nom. sg.
τόδ: ὅδε — this, this here; neut. nom./acc. sg., elided (τόδ’ = τόδε)
τύμβον: τύμβος — burial mound, grave-mound; acc. sg.
τὴν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. sg. ’her’ · also ’it’, of a thing (τὴν = the clothing): fem. acc. sg. · also with a noun, article-like: τὴν ὁδόν ’that journey’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom; fem. acc. sg. (τὴν Ὠκεανὸς τέκε ’whom Oceanus begot’) · also ’the other’, contrasted with a preceding τὴν … μέν: fem. acc. sg. (τὴν δέ ’the other one’) · also article-like with a numeral: ’the one’ (τὴν μὲν ἴαν ’the one portion’)
τὸν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg. ’him’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom, which; masc. acc. sg. (τὸν Ἀλφειὸς τέκε ’whom Alpheus begot’) · also demonstrative adjective with a noun: ’that, the’ (τὸν μῦθον ’that story, message’) · also demonstrative, distributive: masc. acc. sg. ’the one … the other’ (τὸν μὲν … τὸν δ’) · also article-like with a participle: τὸν ἐόντα ’me, the one who am’ · also article-like with a superlative or ordinal: ’the best’ (τὸν ἄριστον), ’the fourth’ (τὸν τέταρτον) · also article-like with a substantivized adjective: ’the like (one)’ (τὸν ὁμοῖον)
τὼ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun); masc. nom. dual: ’the two of them’  ·  also acc. dual, object of a verb of address: τὼ … προσέφη ’spoke to the two of them’ · also relative, nom. dual, ’who (the two)’: τοκῆε δύω, τὼ μὴ γείνασθαι ὄφελλον · also nom. dual with a noun, article-like: ’the two’ (τὼ … θεράποντε)
τῇ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. dat. sg.: ’her, with her’ · also adverbial, ’there, in that place’, pointing back to a place just named (τῇ τόν γε μένον λοχόωντες ’there they lay in wait for him’) · also relative, fem. dat. sg., serving as an instrumental, ’with which’ (ῥάβδον, τῇ τ’ ἀνδρῶν ὄμματα θέλγει ’a wand, with which he charms men’s eyes’), not the personal pronoun · also relative adv., ’where, in the place where’ (τῇ δή μοι ἐείσατο χῶρος ἄριστος) · also adverbial, ’in that (event)’, pointing back to a contest just named: τῇ δ’ αὖτ’ Εὐρύαλος ἀπεκαίνυτο ’in that Euryalus in turn outdid all’ · also relative adv. of manner, with περ: ’in just the way that’ · also adv. of direction, ’thither, that way’ · also with a noun, article-like: fem. dat. sg. ’the’ (τῇ δεκάτῃ ’on the tenth’) · also relative, fem. dat. sg., of respect or means: ’in which, by which’ (ἀγλαΐην, τῇ … κέκασσαι ’the beauty by which you excel’) · also relative, fem. dat. sg., of the person affected: ’upon whom’ (τῇ τις θεὸς ὕπνον ἐπῶρσε ’upon whom some god has stirred up sleep’)
τῶν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); gen. pl. ’of these things, of them’ · also with a noun, article-like: τῶν ἄλλων ἀνέμων ’of the other winds’ · also distributive, ’of the one … of the other’ (τῶν μὲν … τῶν δ’ ’of the one band … of the other’) · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: gen. pl. ’of whom, whose’ (τῶν ὕβρις τε βίη τε … ἵκει ’whose insolence and violence reach’)
τῷ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc./neut. dat. sg.; also relative: ’in which’ · the relative dat. sg. also serves as an instrumental, ’with which’ (τῷ δάμνησι ’with which she overpowers’) · also adverbial ’therefore, and so’ (τῷ οὔ τινα οἶδα ’so I know no one’) · also article-like with a noun: ’that, the same’ (ἤματι τῷ αὐτῷ ’on that same day’) · also demonstrative instrumental, of a thing just named: ’with it’ (τῷ ἀπὸ πείσματ’ ἔκοψα ’with it I cut the cables off’) · also demonstrative of a thing just named, before a preposition: ’it’ (τῷ δ’ ἐν ’and on it’, τῷ δ’ ὑπό ’and beneath it’) · also adverbial, with κε: ’in that case, otherwise’ (τῷ κέ μιν … παύσαμεν ’otherwise we should have stopped him’)
υἱέ: υἱός — son; masc. voc. sg. (Ἀτρέος υἱέ ’son of Atreus’)
υἷες: υἱός — son; masc. nom. pl., epic υἷες (= Attic υἱεῖς)
φίλον: φίλος — dear, one’s own (with kin/body parts serves as a possessive); neut. nom./acc. sg. · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a masculine noun: φίλον υἱόν ’dear son’ · also masc. acc. sg. predicative, agreeing with a pronoun: ’as a friend, welcome’ (φίλον ἐλθεῖν) · also neut. voc. sg., agreeing with τέκος: ’dear (child)’
φίλος: φίλος — dear, dear one; masc. nom. sg. used as voc.: ’friend’ · also plain attributive adjective, not vocative: ’dear’ (φίλος υἱός ’dear son’) · also predicate adjective: ’dear’ (φίλος ἦεν Ἰήσων ’Jason was dear (to her)’)
φαίδιμ: φαίδιμος — gleaming, glorious (epic epithet of heroes); masc. voc. sg., elided (φαίδιμ’ = φαίδιμε)
φαίνετο: φαίνω — show; mid. appear, seem; impf. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented (= ἐφαίνετο)
φεύγετε: φεύγω — flee, run away; pres. 2 pl.: ’you flee’
χαίτας: χαίτη — hair, mane; fem. acc. pl.
χερσὶ: χείρ — hand; fem. dat. pl., epic -σί (= Attic χερσίν)
χρυσείην: χρύσειος — golden, of gold; fem. acc. sg.
χρόα: χρώς — skin, flesh, complexion; acc. sg. χρόα
χρύσεον: χρύσεος — golden; adj., neut. acc. sg., uncontracted (= Attic χρυσοῦν) · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with ὅρμον: ’golden’ (ὅρμον … χρύσεον)
ψυχὰς: ψυχή — life, spirit, soul; fem. acc. pl.
ψυχὴ: ψυχή — soul, spirit, ghost; fem. nom. sg.
ψυχὴν: ψυχή — life, soul, life-breath; acc. sg.
ἀγγελίης: ἀγγελίη — message, tidings, bidding; fem. gen. sg. (Ionic η)
ἀγηγέραθ: ἀγείρω — gather, assemble; plpf. 3 pl. mid./pass., epic -ατο elided (ἀγηγέραθ’ = ἀγηγέρατο), τ>θ before rough breathing: ’were gathered’
ἀγορήσατο: ἀγοράομαι — speak in the assembly; aor. 3 sg. mid.
ἀγχίμολον: ἀγχίμολος — coming near, close at hand; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’close by, hard upon’
ἀγόρευον: ἀγορεύω — speak, say, declare; impf. 3 pl.
ἀγῶνι: ἀγών — gathering, the place where people gather for the games; masc. dat. sg.
ἀκτῇ: ἀκτή — ground grain, grist (a different word from ἀκτή ’shore’); fem. dat. sg., Ionic -ῃ, of means
ἀλεύεται: ἀλέομαι — avoid, shun, take care not (to); aor. subj. 3 sg. mid., short vowel (= ἀλεύηται), perhaps a fut.; + inf.
ἀλλήλους: ἀλλήλων — one another; reciprocal pron., masc. acc. pl.
ἀλλήλῃσιν: ἀλλήλων — one another; fem. dat. pl., epic -ῃσι(ν)
ἀλόχοιο: ἄλοχος — wife, bedfellow; fem. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
ἀμφ: ἀμφί (elided ἀμφ’) — around, about, concerning; + dat. · also + acc., ’around, with, accompanying’ (ἀμφ’ Ὀδυσῆα ’with, around Odysseus’) · also + gen., ’about, concerning’ (ἀμφ’ Ἄρεος φιλότητος ’about the love of Ares’) · also with ὀστεόφιν, ’around’ (ἀμφ’ ὀστεόφιν θὶς ’a heap around the bones’)
ἀμφιμέδοντα: Ἀμφιμέδων — Amphimedon, a suitor; masc. acc. sg.
ἀμφὶ: ἀμφί — on both sides, around, about; prep./adv. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἀμφὶ ... βάλλομεν = ἀμφιβάλλομεν ’we threw around, embraced’)
ἀμύμονα: ἀμύμων — blameless, excellent (traditional sense; exact meaning uncertain); adj., fem. acc. sg. · also masc. acc. sg.: ἀμύμονα Λαοδάμαντα ’blameless Laodamas’ · also neut. acc. pl., substantival: ’blameless things’ (ἀμύμονα εἰδῇ ’knows blameless things’)
ἀμύμονος: ἀμύμων — blameless, excellent (an old epithet whose exact force is uncertain); gen. sg.
ἀνά: ἀνά — up, up along; prep. + acc., or adv. · also as preverb in tmesis (ἀνά … ἔβαινον = ἀνέβαινον ’mounted’); acute kept before an enclitic
ἀναΐξαντες: ἀναΐσσω — spring up, rush up; aor. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’having sprung up’
ἀνθρώπους: ἄνθρωπος — human being, man; acc. pl.
ἀντεβόλησας: ἀντιβολέω — meet, encounter (+ dat.); aor. 2 sg.: ’you have met’
ἀντιλόχοιο: Ἀντίλοχος — Antilochus, son of Nestor; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
ἀντιόωσα: ἀντιάω — come to meet, partake of; pres. part. fem. nom. sg., epic diectasis (= Attic ἀντιῶσα), + gen.
ἀρίστη: ἄριστος — best; superl., fem. nom. sg.
ἀργείων: Ἀργεῖοι — the Argives, i.e. the Greeks; gen. pl.
ἀργεϊφόντης: Ἀργεϊφόντης — ’Argeïphontes’, standing epithet of Hermes, conventionally ’slayer of Argus’; masc. nom. sg.; the meaning is disputed, not actually known
ἀργεῖοι: Ἀργεῖοι — the Argives, i.e. the Greeks; masc. nom. pl.
ἀσφοδελὸν: ἀσφοδελός — of asphodel, asphodel-covered; masc. acc. sg. (with λειμῶνα)
ἀτρεΐδαο: Ἀτρεΐδης — son of Atreus, i.e. Agamemnon; gen. sg., epic (-αο = Attic -ου)
ἀτρεΐδη: Ἀτρεΐδης — son of Atreus; masc. voc. sg.
ἀχαιοί: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, the Greeks; masc. nom. pl.
ἀχαιούς: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, the Greeks; masc. acc. pl.
ἀχαιοὶ: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, the Greeks; masc. nom. pl.
ἀχαιῶν: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, the Greeks; gen. pl.
ἀχιλῆος: Ἀχιλλεύς — Achilles; masc. gen. sg., single-λ epic (= Attic Ἀχιλλέως)
ἀχνυμένη: ἄχνυμαι — be grieved, sorrow; pres. part. mid. fem. nom. sg.: ’grieving’
ἁλίοιο: ἅλιος — of the sea, belonging to the sea; adj., masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου), epithet of γέρων ’the old man of the sea’
ἁλίῃσιν: ἅλιος — of the sea; fem. dat. pl., epic -ῃσι (= Attic -αις), agreeing with ψαμάθοις: ’sands of the sea’
ἁλὸς: ἅλς — sea, salt water; fem. gen. sg. · also masc. gen. sg., with the masc. adjective πολιοῖο: ’of the grey sea’ (ἁλὸς πολιοῖο)
ἁλῶναι: ἁλίσκομαι — be caught, be taken; aor. inf. ἁλῶναι
ἁπάντων: ἅπας — all, the whole of; neut. gen. pl.: ’of all (ills)’ · also masc. gen. pl., in comparison: ’of all (mortals)’ · also gen. pl. with a noun: ’of all (men)’
ἄγε: ἄγε — come now!; interjectional imper. of ἄγω, 2 sg. · also ἄγω — lead; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἦγε): ’led’ · also ἄγω — lead; pres. imper. 2 sg.: ’lead’ (μή μ’ ἄγε κεῖσ’ ’do not lead me there’)
ἄλγε: ἄλγος — pain, grief; neut. nom./acc. pl. (ἄλγεα, elided ἄλγε’)
ἄλλαι: ἄλλος — other, another; fem. nom. pl.
ἄλλοι: ἄλλος — other, another; masc. nom. pl.
ἄμβροτα: ἄμβροτος — immortal, divine, undying; adj., neut. acc. pl., epic (= ἀθάνατος)
ἄνθρωποι: ἄνθρωπος — human being, man; masc. nom. pl.
ἄρα: ἄρα — so, as it turned out, then; inferential particle
ἄριστοι: ἄριστος — best; superl., masc. nom. pl.
ἄριστος: ἀγαθός — good; superlative ἄριστος ’best’; adj., masc. nom. sg.
ἅμ: ἅμα (elided ἅμ’) — together with, at the same time as; adv./prep. + dat.
ἐγείρει: ἐγείρω — wake, rouse; pres. 3 sg. act.
ἐθέλει: ἐθέλω — wish, be willing, intend; pres. 3 sg.
ἐκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as adverb or preverb in tmesis, no case expressed: ’out’ (ἐκ δ’ ἔβαν ’and out they stepped’)
ἐμοὶ: ἐγώ — I; dat. sg.: ’to, for me’ · also dat. of possession: ’mine is, I have’ (ἐμοὶ δ’ ὄνομα ’my name is’)
ἐν: ἐν — in, on, among; + dat.; also used as an adverb, ’in it, there’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐν … βάλῃ = ἐμβάλῃ ’cast in’; ἐν … χεῦον = ἔγχεον ’pour in’)
ἐξ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐξ … ἕντο = ἐξέντο, from ἐξίημι ’send out, put away (desire)’)
ἐπ: ἐπί (elided ἐπ’) — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐπ’ … χεῦε = ἐπέχευε ‘poured upon’) · also + dat., of time: ’in, within’ (ἐπ’ ἤματι ’in a day’) · also + acc., ’in pursuit of, after’ (ἐπ’ ἀγροτέρας ’after wild (goats)’) · also + dat., ’in favour of, on behalf of’ (ἐπ’ Ἴρῳ ἦρα φέρων ’showing favour to Irus’) · also + acc. of time: ’for’ (ἐπ’ ἦμαρ ’for a day’) · also + gen., of place: ’at, on’ (ἐπ’ ἐσχατιῆς ’at the edge’) · also + dat., of place: ’at, by’ (ἐπ’ Ὠκεανῷ ’at Oceanus’)
ἐπέσπον: ἐφέπω — follow upon, pursue, meet with; aor. 3 pl. ἐπέσπον: ’met with, incurred’ (κακὸν οἶτον ἐπέσπον ’met an evil doom’) · also aor. 1 sg. (same form): ’I met with’ (πότμον ἐπέσπον ’I met my doom’)
ἐπισπεῖν: ἐφέπω — follow, meet, come upon (+ acc., of fate); aor. inf. ἐπισπεῖν
ἐπὶ: ἐπί — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as adverb, no case expressed: ’to it, over it; besides’ (θεοὶ δ’ ἐπὶ μάρτυροι ’witnesses to it’; ἐπὶ κτέρεα κτερεΐξαι ’besides’) · also + dat., ’beyond, over and above, more than’ (ἐπὶ γαστέρι κύντερον ’more shameless than the belly’) · also adverb of sequence, ’next, thereupon’ (ἦλθε δ’ ἐπὶ ψυχή ’and next came the soul’) · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb: ἐπὶ … τέταλτο = ἐπιτέταλτο ’was laid upon, entrusted’ · also + acc. of time: ’for, over’ (ἐπὶ χρόνον ’for a time’) · also + dat., ’in charge of, over’ (ἐπὶ κτεάτεσσιν ’over my possessions’) · also + dat., of purpose: ’for’ (ἐπὶ δόρπῳ ’for supper’) · also + dat., of the occasion: ’at, over’ (ἐπὶ ῥηθέντι δικαίῳ ’at a fair remark’)
ἐρρώσαντο: ῥώομαι — move with vigour, dart, rush; aor. 3 pl. mid. (of the knees): ’moved briskly’
ἐσθλόν: ἐσθλός — good, noble, brave; masc. acc. sg. or neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἐϋφρονέων: εὐφρονέω (epic ἐϋφρονέω) — be well-minded, be well-disposed; pres. part. masc. nom. sg., uncontracted (= Attic εὐφρονῶν): ’well-disposed’
ἑκὰς: ἑκάς — far, far off; adv. · also prep. + gen.: ’far from’ (νηῶν ἑκὰς ’far from the ships’)
ἑπτὰ: ἑπτά — seven; numeral, indecl. (ἑπτὰ καὶ δέκα ’seventeen’)
ἑρμείας: Ἑρμείας — Hermes, epic form of Ἑρμῆς; nom. sg.
ἑρμῆς: Ἑρμῆς — Hermes; masc. nom. sg. (the plain form, beside the fuller Ἑρμείας used elsewhere in the same part)
ἑτάρων: ἑταῖρος (epic ἕταρος) — companion, comrade; masc. gen. pl. (= Attic ἑταίρων)
ἔβαν: βαίνω — go, walk; aor. 3 pl., epic (= Attic ἔβησαν)
ἔγνω: γιγνώσκω — come to know, learn, perceive; aor. 3 sg., no augment
ἔην: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἦν)
ἔλλαβε: λαμβάνω — take, win, get; aor. 3 sg., augmented with double λ, epic (= Attic ἔλαβε)
ἔμελλεν: μέλλω — be about to, be destined to; impf. 3 sg., augmented (root μελλ-, consonant-initial; unaugmented μέλλε(ν)): ’was going to, was destined’
ἔμεναι: εἰμί — be; pres. inf., epic (= Attic εἶναι)
ἔμμεναι: εἰμί — be; pres. inf., epic (= Attic εἶναι)
ἔν: ἐν — in, on; preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἔν … φῦ = ἐνέφυ ’took firm hold’) · also prep. + dat., ’on’, accented before the enclitic τε (ἔν τε τάπησι ’on rugs’)
ἔνθα: ἔνθα — there, then; adverb of place or time · also used relatively, continuing a clause: ’where’ (ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’) · also doubled, ἔνθα καὶ ἔνθα ’this way and that’
ἔνι: ἐν — in; prep. + dat., postpositive with anastrophe, accent thrown back after its noun (δήμῳ ἔνι = ἐν δήμῳ) · also = ἔνεστι, ἔνεισι (ἔνι with no case): ’there is, there are in it/among them’ (ἄνδρες νηῶν ἔνι τέκτονες ’men, shipwrights, are among them’)
ἔξοχα: ἔξοχος — outstanding, preeminent; neut. pl. used as adv.: ’above all, outstandingly’
ἔπι: ἐπί — on, upon, over; prep. + dat., placed after its noun with anastrophe: ἑοῖς ἔπι ’upon his own (possessions)’ · also + gen., postpositive with anastrophe, of direction: ’toward’ (νήσου ἔπι Ψυρίης ’toward the island of Psyria’) · also as adverb with no case expressed, intensifying repetition: ’besides, again’ (ἔπι δεύτερον αὖτις ’a second time, once more’) · also = ἔπεστι, accented on the first syllable when it stands for the verb: ’there is (upon)’ · also as preverb in tmesis, placed after its object: ἔπι … ὦρσεν = ἐπῶρσεν ’stirred up (against)’ · also + gen., postpositive with anastrophe, of place: ’on, upon’ (οὐδοῦ ἔπι ξεστοῦ ’on the polished threshold’) · also + acc., postpositive with anastrophe, of place: ’over, upon’ (γαῖαν ἔπι ’over the earth’)
ἔργον: ἔργον — deed, work, task; neut. acc. sg. · also neut. nom. sg., subject of an impersonal verb (κακὸν … ἔργον τε ἔπος τε μελέτω ’let no evil deed or word be a care’) · also neut. nom. sg., in apposition/predicative, naming a maker: ἔργον Ἡφαίστοιο ’the work of Hephaestus’ · also neut. nom. sg., subject of a passive verb: ’work’ (τόδε ἔργον ἀέξεται ’this work grows’)
ἔσσεται: εἰμί — be; fut. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἔσται)
ἔστησαν: ἵστημι — set up, stand; aor. 3 pl. of ἔστην, intransitive: ’took their stand, stood’
ἔσχοντο: ἔχω — have, hold; mid. aor. ἐσχόμην, intransitive: be held, hold oneself back; aor. 3 pl. mid.: ’were held, held back’
ἔφαθ: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid. (ἔφατο, elided ἔφαθ’, τ>θ before rough breathing)
ἔχε: ἔχω — have, hold; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= Attic εἶχε) · also pres. imper. 2 sg.: ’hold, keep’ (ἔχε σιγῇ μῦθον ’keep the word in silence’)
ἔχονται: ἔχω (mid.) — hold oneself, cling; pres. mid. 3 pl., + πρός and dat.: ’cling to one another’
ἕλικας: ἕλιξ — twisted, curved (of cattle’s horns); fem. acc. pl.
ἕσσαν: ἕννυμι — clothe; aor. 3 pl. ἕσσαν, epic (Attic ἠμφίεσαν): ’they clothed (her) in’, with acc. of the garment
ἠδέ: ἠδέ — and; epic conjunction, accented before an enclitic
ἠελίοιο: Ἠέλιος — the Sun (god); gen. sg., epic (-οιο = Attic Ἡλίου)
ἠῶθεν: ἠώς — dawn; adv. ἠῶθεν, -θεν suffix ’from’: ’at dawn’
ἡμεῖς: ἐγώ (pl. ἡμεῖς) — I, we; nom. pl. ’we’
ἡφαίστοιο: Ἥφαιστος — Hephaestus, god of the forge; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
ἤδη: ἤδη — now, already, at once; adv.
ἤλυθ: ἔρχομαι — come, go; aor. 3 sg., elided (ἤλυθ’ = ἤλυθε), epic (= Attic ἦλθε)
ἤματα: ἦμαρ — day; neut. acc. pl., acc. of time: ’all the days, every day’ · also neut. nom. pl., subject: ’the days’ (νύκτες τε καὶ ἤματα φθίνουσιν)
ἤνυσεν: ἀνύω — accomplish, achieve, complete (a distance/journey); aor. 3 sg.
ἤϊσαν: εἶμι — go; impf. 3 pl., epic (= Attic ᾖσαν): ’went’
ἥδε: ὅδε, ἥδε, τόδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., fem. nom. sg.
ἦ: ἦ — truly, verily; affirming particle · also interrogative particle introducing an earnest question · also = ἤ ’or’, in the correlative ἠέ … ἦ ’whether … or’ · also ἠμί — say, speak; unaugmented aor./impf. 3 sg. (= ἔφη), closing or introducing direct speech: ’he/she said’ (ἦ ῥα ’so he said’) · also ’or’, the second alternative of a pair of questions with no preceding ἠέ: ζώει … ἦ τέθνηκε ’alive or dead’; ἢ ἔτ’ ἔχει … ἦ μιν ἀτιμάζουσιν ’whether … or’
ἦδος: ἦδος — pleasure, delight; neut. nom. sg.
ἦμαρ: ἦμαρ — day (epic for ἡμέρα); neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἦρχε: ἄρχω — begin, rule; impf. 3 sg., + gen. ’began (the speaking)’ · also ’go first, lead the way’ (no gen.): ἦρχε δ’ Ἀθήνη ’and Athena went first, led the way’ · also + gen. of the way: ἦρχε ὁδοῖο ’led the way’ · also absolute: ’ruled, was king’
ἧς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; fem. gen. sg. · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whose, of whom/which (fem. gen. sg.)
ἰδὼν: ὁράω (aor. stem εἰδ-) — see; aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg., epic (= Attic ἰδών): ’seeing’
ἰθὺς: ἰθύς — straight; prep. + gen. (epic = Attic εὐθύς): ’straight towards’ · also adv., no case expressed: ’straight, straight on’
ἰφθίμοισιν: ἴφθιμος — stout, strong, mighty; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις)
ἴσαν: εἶμι — go, come; impf. 3 pl., epic: ’used to go, come’ · also as a simple narrative past, ’went’ (μνηστῆρες … ἴσαν ’the suitors went’), not necessarily iterative · also οἶδα — know; unaugmented plup. 3 pl. with impf. sense, epic (= Attic ᾔδεσαν): ’they knew’ (τὰ δ’ οὐκ ἴσαν ’they did not know’)
ἵκοντο: ἱκνέομαι — come, arrive at, reach; aor. 3 pl.; with short ι (by metre) unaugmented; where the metre makes the ι long, augmented (the spelling cannot show it)
ὀδυσῆϊ: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; masc. dat. sg., epic Ὀδυσῆϊ (single σ, diaeresis; = Ὀδυσσῆϊ, Attic Ὀδυσσεῖ)
ὀκτωκαιδεκάτῃ: ὀκτωκαιδέκατος — eighteenth; fem. dat. sg. (sc. ἡμέρῃ), ’on the eighteenth (day)’
ὀλοφυρόμεναι: ὀλοφύρομαι — lament, wail; pres. part. mid./dep. fem. nom. pl.
ὀπίσσω: ὀπίσσω — behind; in Homer also ’hereafter, in time to come’; adv. · also ’back, home again’, of return (οἴκαδ’ ὀπίσσω ’back home’)
ὀπὶ: ὄψ — voice; fem. dat. sg. (ὀπὶ καλῇ ’with a beautiful voice’)
ὀρώρει: ὄρνυμι — rouse; (intrans.) arise, spring up; pluperf. 3 sg., unaugmented: ’had sprung up’
ὀστέ: ὀστέον (pl. ὀστέα) — bone; neut. nom. pl., elided (ὀστέ’ = ὀστέα)
ὀστέα: ὀστέον — bone; neut. nom./acc. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic ὀστᾶ)
ὁμῶς: ὁμῶς — alike, in like manner, equally; adv.
ὃς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.) · also plain demonstrative, ’he’ (ὃς γὰρ δεύτατος ἦλθεν), not a relative
ὄλεθρον: ὄλεθρος — destruction, ruin, death; acc. sg.
ὄνομ: ὄνομα — name; neut. nom. sg., elided (ὄνομ’ = ὄνομα), subject of λίπηται: ’his name’ · also neut. acc. sg., object: ’a name’ (ὄνομ’ εὕρεο ’find a name’) · also neut. nom. sg., predicate with ἔστω: ’a name’
ὅ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. sg.; with γε: ’he’ · also relative, masc. nom. sg., accented before an enclitic: ’who’ (ὅ κε ... ἐφείη) · also = ὅτι ’that’; εἰς ὅ ’until’ · also relative, neut. nom./acc. sg.: ’which’ (ὅ οἱ πέρι δῶκεν Ἀθήνη ’which Athena gave her beyond others’) · also masc. nom. sg. pronoun ’he’ without γε, accented before an enclitic (ὅ σφιν ’he … to them’)
ὅθι: ὅθι — where; epic relative adverb (= Attic οὗ)
ὅς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.) · also with τις, an indirect interrogative: οὐκ οἶδ’ ὅς τις ’I know not who’ · also with τις, indefinite relative: ὅς τις … φάγοι ’whoever should eat’
ὅσσαι: ὅσος (epic ὅσσος) — as much as, as many as; fem. nom. pl., epic geminated form ὅσσαι (= ὅσαι)
ὅτε: ὅτε — when; temporal conjunction · also ’since, now that’ (ὅτε πρότερός γε πύθοιτο ’since he learned of it first’) · also with the optative, hypothetical/conditional: ’if ever, whenever’ (ὅτε ... ἵκοι ’if ever such need should come upon me’) · also with the subjunctive, general: ’whenever’ (ὅτε στείχῃσ’ ἀνὰ ἄστυ ’whenever she goes through the town’) · also with the optative, iterative in past time: ’whenever’ (ὅτε μέλλοι ’whenever he was about to’) · also with the pres. indic., ’whereas, when’ (ὅτε τ’ ἄλλοι ἅπαξ θνῄσκουσ’ ἄνθρωποι ’whereas other men die only once’) · also in ὅτε μή, ’unless, except when’ (ὅτε μὴ θεὸς … θείη ’unless a god should make’)
ὑπνώοντας: ὑπνόω — sleep, be asleep; pres. part. act. masc. acc. pl., diectasis (uncontracted): ’sleeping’
ὑπὸ: ὑπό — under, beneath; prep. + dat./acc.; also used as an adverb, ’beneath’ · also as preverb in tmesis (ὑπὸ … ἐδήσατο = ὑπεδήσατο ’bound beneath’) · also adverbial, of breeding: ’begotten under, born of’ (ὑπὸ δ’ ἡμίονοι ’and under them [the mares], mules’) · also + dat., marking the agent with a passive verb: ’by’ (ὑπὸ μνηστῆρσιν δαμείη ’be overcome by the suitors’) · also + gen., ’from under, beneath’ (ὑπὸ στέρνοιο) · also + gen., marking agent with a passive verb/participle beyond dying, ’by’: μεγάλου ὑπὸ κύματος ἀρθείς ’lifted up by a great wave’ · also + gen., of cause: ὑπὸ ῥιπῆς ’at the rush (of the throw)’
ὠκεανοῦ: Ὠκεανός — Oceanus, the world-encircling river; masc. gen. sg.
ὡς: ὡς — as, how, that, when; with the optative introduces a wish: ’so may…’ (unaccented; accented ὥς / ὣς is ’thus’) · also ὡς + unaugmented ὄφελον + inf., an unfulfillable wish: ’would that...’ · also ὡς + opt., a purpose clause (= ἵνα): ’so that’ (ὡς τὸν χόλον ἐξακέσαιτο ’so that he might appease the anger’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. + inf.: ’how (good, etc.) it is to...’ (ὡς ἀγαθὸν ... λιπέσθαι ’how good a thing it is to be left behind’) · also plain ὡς + indic., ’as’ (ὡς σὺ κελεύεις ’as you command’) or ’how’ in an indirect question (ὡς ἐπὶ πόντον ἐλεύσομαι ’how I shall come upon the sea’) · also ὡς ἄν + subj., a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὡς ἂν μὴ κλαίουσα κατὰ χρόα καλὸν ἰάπτῃς ’so that you might not mar your fair skin with weeping’) · also ὡς δ’ ὅτε introducing an epic simile, ’as when’, its clause taking indic. or ἄν/κε + subj. for a general case: ὡς δ’ ὅτ’ ἂν ... φανήῃ ’as when ... should appear’ · also comparative ’like’, placed after the noun it compares (ἀνέμου ὡς πνοιή ’like a blast of wind’) · also ὡς εἰ ’as if, like’ (ὡς εἰ πτερὸν ἠὲ νόημα ’as if a wing or a thought’) · also ὡς + ἄν + opt., potential, ’as, in the way that, such as’ (ὡς οὐκ ἂν ἔλποιο ’such as you would not expect’) · also introducing a simile with the subj. and no ἄν: ’as when (a woman weeps)’ · also in an asseveration with fut. indic., ’as surely as’ (ὡς οὐκ ὀφθαλμόν γ’ ἰήσεται ’as surely as nothing will heal the eye’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. with a finite verb: ’how (dear) he is’ (ὡς ὅδε … φίλος … ἐστίν) · also ὡς ἄν + subj., of manner: ’as’ (ὡς ἂν ἐγὼ εἴπω ’as I shall say’) · also comparative ’like’, standing before its noun (ὡς νυκτερίς ’like a bat’) · also ὡς ὅθ’ (= ὡς ὅτε), ’as when’, comparing with an occasion in the past (ὡς ὅθ’ ὑπὸ Τροίην ’as when beneath Troy’) · also introducing an indirect statement after a verb of saying: ’that, how’ (εἴποιμ’ ὡς … ἔρχομαι ’I might tell how I am coming’) · also ὡς ἄν + opt., a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὡς ἄν τίς σε … μακαρίζοι ’so that someone … would call you blessed’) · also ὡς + participle, ’as one who’ (ὡς ἐκ θανάτοιο φυγόντα ’as one escaped from death’) · also ὡς ἄν + subj., a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὡς ἂν … ἔρχησθον ’so that you two may go’) · also ὡς = ’to, toward’ + acc. of a person (ὡς τὸν ὁμοῖον ’to the like’) · also exclamatory ὡς + finite verb: ’how’ (ὡς ὁ μολοβρὸς … ἀγορεύει ’how the glutton talks’)
ὣς: ὥς — thus, so; adverb (accented, distinct from unaccented ὡς ’as’; = Attic οὕτως) · also postpositive after its noun (anastrophe), = comparative ὡς ’as, like’: ὄρνις δ’ ὥς ’like a bird’ · also introducing a wish with the optative: ’so may…’ (ὣς ἔμ’ ἀϊστώσειαν ’so may they make me vanish’)
ὥς: ὥς — thus, so; also (with κε/ἄν + subj.) ’so that, in order that’; adverb/conjunction · also introducing an indirect question: ’how’ (ὥς κε νέηται ’how he is to return’, after φράσσεται) · or ὡς ’as’, accented before enclitic τε · also causal, ’since, seeing that’ (ὥς οἱ ἐναργὲς ὄνειρον ἐπέσσυτο ’since a vivid dream had come upon her’) · also with κεν + opt., purpose: ’so that’ (ὥς κεν … γένοιτο ’so that he might become’) · also ὥς ’just as’, in ὥς περ (accented before enclitic περ) (ὥς περ ὑπέστης ’just as you promised’) · also ὡς ’as’, accented before enclitic με (ὥς με κελεύεις ’as you bid me’) · also postpositive after its noun, comparative ’like’ (οἰωνῶν ὥς ’like birds’) · also ὡς ’as’, accented before enclitic τοι (ὥς τοι ἐγὼν ἐρέω ’as I shall tell you’) · also correlative ’so’ answering ὅπως, introducing a wish with the opt., accented before the enclitic τοι: ’so may’ (ὥς τοι Ζεὺς τελέσειεν ’so may Zeus fulfil it for you’) · also with a plain subj. (no κε/ἄν), purpose: ’so that’ (ὥς τοι δῶρ’ ἀποπέμψω ’so that I may send you the gifts’) · also ὥς accented before enclitic οἱ, of measure: ’as much as’ (ὥς οἱ χεῖρες ἐχάνδανον ’as much as his hands could hold’) · also exclamatory, ’how’, accented before the enclitic τις (ὥς τις θαρσαλέος … ἐσσι ’how bold you are’) · also with the plain optative (no κε/ἄν), purpose, accented before the enclitic μιν: ’so that’ (ὥς μιν ψυχὴ λίποι ’so that life should leave him’) · also ὡς ’as, how’, accented before enclitic μοι (ὥς μοι ἰνδάλλεται ’as it seems to me’) · also ὡς ’how’, introducing a narrated event, accented before the enclitic μιν (ὥς μιν θηρεύοντ’ ἔλασεν ’how he struck him as he hunted’) · also ὡς ’as, like’, accented before enclitic τις (ὥς τις ’like some’)
ὧν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; masc./neut. gen. pl. · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: of whom, whose; gen. pl., partitive (τοὺς δ’ ὧν ἐθέλει ’whomever he wishes’), not the possessive
ῥ: ἄρα (weakened ῥα, elided ῥ’) — then, indeed, so; inferential particle
ῥάβδον: ῥάβδος — wand, rod, staff; fem. acc. sg. (Hermes’s standing attribute)
ῥοὰς: ῥοή — stream, flow; fem. acc. pl.
